input: The settler under consideration is a gravity unit that has been designed to remove sand from a process stream, and its sizing is based on the widely used overflow-rate method. The throughput of the unit is 303 m3 h-1, and the design overflow rate that has been adopted is 1.74 m h-1, a value taken from a vendor rule developed for this particular solid. The required plan area is obtained by dividing the throughput by the overflow rate, so that 303 m3 h-1 divided by 1.74 m h-1 gives a plan area of 174 m2 for the settler. It is important to note, however, that the overflow-rate basis has an important limitation: no settling test has actually been carried out on the real slurry, which means that the design rate has not been validated against the behaviour of the material that the unit will really treat. As a result, the plan area of 174 m2 should be regarded as an estimate that rests entirely on the vendor rule, and factors such as the particle size distribution of the sand, the solids loading, and short-circuiting near the inlet could all cause the performance of the installed unit to differ appreciably from the design intention, whether for better or for worse. For these reasons, the sizing should be understood as a first estimate that will need to be revisited once test data on the actual slurry become available at some point in the future.
target: A gravity settler removes sand from a process stream. The design overflow rate is 1.74 m h-1 at a throughput of 303 m3 h-1. Plan area follows from the overflow-rate definition: the area is the throughput divided by the overflow rate. Thus 303 m3 h-1 divided by 1.74 m h-1 gives a plan area of 174 m2. The overflow rate is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the rate has not been checked against the slurry as fed, and the plan area of 174 m2 stands on the vendor rule alone. The rule takes no account of the sand grading as fed, of the solids loading, or of short-circuiting at the inlet, and each of these moves the rate a working settler achieves. Plan area is the sizing variable because the overflow rate is stated per unit of area: the liquid rises through the settler at the overflow rate, and a particle that settles faster than the liquid rises reaches the floor of the unit, while a particle that settles more slowly is carried out with the overflow. The stated basis therefore fixes the area arithmetically and leaves its adequacy untested. Any margin for the untested basis has to be added to the area as a separate decision; nothing in the overflow rate, the throughput, or the division between them supplies one. The design as stated also leaves the plan dimensions, the depth, and the inlet and outlet arrangements open, and each of these affects how closely the installed unit approaches the uniform upward flow that the overflow-rate definition assumes. The figure to carry forward is a settler of the computed area, sized by a rule that the feed material has not yet confirmed.
